chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the purification of a woman in nifās when she becomes pure, while she is unable to perform istinjāʾ with water, such that if she were to perform istinjāʾ she would become injured. Is there a concession for her to perform wudu (ablution) externally and dry it with cotton or with a cloth? He said: “Yes. Let her cleanse the inside with cotton or with a cloth.”

key_terms.بِخِرْقَةٍ: with a cloth, used here as a means of cleansing
key_terms.بِقُطْنٍ: with cotton, used here as a means of cleansing
key_terms.تَسْتَنْجِيَ: to cleanse the private area after discharge or impurity
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: a legal concession granted due to hardship or harm
key_terms.طَهُورِ: ritual purification in the context of becoming clean after nifās

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman after nifās if using water for istinjāʾ would cause harm?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the taharah of a woman after nifās when using water for internal cleansing would cause harm. It permits a concession in method, allowing external wudu (ablution) and internal cleansing with cotton or cloth, showing consideration for hardship in ritual purity rulings.
